ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(g05): add OpenGalaxea G0.5 policy integration (#4445)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(g05): add OpenGalaxea G0.5 policy integration  (#4445)

* Add the OpenGalaxea G0.5 policy

Native port of G0.5 (Qwen3.5-2B VLA) as policy.type=g05 on Transformers' Qwen3.5
backbone: action expert, flow-matching head, ActionCodec and unified CoT/action
decode, with no OpenGalaxea, Hydra or OmegaConf dependency.

- Codec and tokenizer live in their own modules; the tokenizer and ActionCodec are
  saved as safetensors processor artifacts.
- The relative-action anchor is held while a chunk is in flight.
- The integration code and G0.5 model cards carry the G0.5 Community License.

* Reset the postprocessor when a task change drops the queued actions

In the synchronous rollout, dropping the queued actions on a task change now also
resets the postprocessor, so a stateful step such as the relative-action anchor
starts from the new chunk.

* Fine-tune G0.5 base on new robots from their dataset stats, joints and cameras

- policy.embodiment is a free-text robot name; the released names keep their slot tables.
- Joint slots come from the dataset's joint names (state_slots/action_slots override them),
  and camera_order maps dataset cameras to image slots (null leaves one empty).
- Normalization uses lerobot's normalization_mapping with the dataset's own stats.
- Recipe pipelines load from a Hub repo id, with fewer host syncs.

* Rotate task_aug rephrasings through the training recipe into the G0.5 prompt

The training renderer passed the dataset task as an explicit override, so ${task}
never used task_aug rephrasings for any recipe-based policy. It now passes it as the
fallback (runtime override, then task_aug, then the dataset task).

* Train G0.5 like upstream

- Type-checked under the repository mypy ruleset; flash-linear-attention is recommended.
- Upstream's sample mix of CoT, subtask-as-task and plain samples; the CoT text is cut
  before its Action segment.
- ActionCodec targets leave out body parts the robot does not have (dropout_noop_parts).
- The System 2 chain of thought is selectable (subtask, or bbox and subtask), and
  action codes are masked while it is sampled.
- proprio_dropout_p (default 0.2, upstream's mlp_dropout) drops the state token in training.
- The flow loss repeats the action cache in the targets' row order and detaches the
  VLM KV (knowledge insulation, upstream's default).
- The docs use generic robot and dataset names.

* Configure G0.5 precision with policy.dtype and read recipe_path once

- Precision uses the shared PreTrainedConfig.dtype (bfloat16 or float32) instead of
  model_weights_to_bf16.
- recipe_path is read into the inline recipe when the config is built and then
  cleared, so a saved checkpoint keeps its recipe and the config builds on a base install.

* Check G0.5 joint_signs against the robot's joints after the slots size them

The length check ran in __post_init__ against the checkpoint's raw_state_dim, so
fine-tuning g05_base (14 joints) on a 6-joint arm with 6 joint_signs failed before
the dataset could resize the slots.

* Remove dead G0.5 code

- The ActionCodec's own training objective: lerobot only encodes and decodes with the
  shipped codec.
- The FP32 output-projection cast: the VLM ties its logits to input_proj.
- Inference metadata and batch fields nothing reads, and predict_action_chunk_with_runtime.
- checkpoint_profile and return_continuous_action, config fields that were only validated.
- Unreachable branches: per-sample action encoding, the optional decode mask, and
  attribute fallbacks on objects that always have them.

* Add the G0.5 policy README and refresh the docs

- The README is symlinked from the package (paper link and citation), and G0.5 model
  cards link to the guide.
- Stale references to removed APIs, checkpoint profiles and recipe_path are fixed.

* Simplify G0.5 around the shared lerobot pieces

- Flow times, noise and training inputs come from the shared flow-matching helpers
  (sample_beta, sample_noise, make_flow_matching_inputs; same values). Only the
  pi-convention path the checkpoints use is kept, with upstream's Euler loop: its time
  stays in the model dtype, which the shared euler_integrate does not reproduce in BF16.
- Author samples are built by a processor function, prepare_g05_policy_batch, instead
  of a weightless policy proxy.
- The policy calls its backend directly, and the ActionCodec loads in one place.
- use_language_recipe is read directly, the ActionCodec part/marker list is computed
  once, and the prompt templates share their prefix.

* Return G0.5's System 2 subtask and boxes as the policy prediction

* Retarget lerobot-train's relative_actions_processor override to G0.5's relative step, so relative-action runs resume

* Port G0.5's Qwen3.5 linear attention, vision rotary and position embeddings to transformers 5.22

ns0:entry.ns0:title: perf(datasets): stream-copy videos when deleting episodes (#4498)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
perf(datasets): stream-copy videos when deleting episodes (#4498)

* perf(datasets): stream-copy videos when deleting episodes

delete_episodes re-encoded every kept frame of any video file that mixed kept
and deleted episodes. That work is redundant for datasets written by LeRobot:
DatasetWriter encodes one video per episode and concatenate_video_files joins
them through ffmpeg's concat demuxer in stream-copy mode, so the first frame of
every episode in a packed file starts a closed GOP.

Select and remux the encoded packets instead when every boundary is GOP-aligned.
Alignment is verified rather than assumed, so files packed by other tools still
fall back to the existing re-encode path.

Measured on a 79-episode unitree_g1 dataset (640x480 h264 @ 50fps), dropping 32
episodes: for the three ego_view files 220.6s -> 0.9s, output 364MB -> 306MB,
and the kept frames are now bit-identical to the source instead of a second
lossy generation.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix(datasets): harden stream-copy episode deletion

- Copy codec parameters with add_stream_from_template(opaque=True). Without it, AV1 input (decoded by libdav1d) crashed because no encoder of that name exists, so the fast path raised instead of falling back.
- Only cut at keyframes that are presented before every later packet and after every earlier one. Open-GOP keyframes followed by leading pictures were accepted and produced wrong frames; they now fall back to re-encoding.
- Validate boundaries from packet metadata in a first demux pass and stream the selected packets in a second, so memory no longer scales with the video file size.
- Test stream copy for h264, hevc and libsvtav1, including frame count and timestamp continuity, and add an open-GOP rejection test.

* docs(datasets): shorten stream-copy docstring

* fix(datasets): sort stream-copy frame ranges internally

* style(datasets): format stream-copy range validation

* test(datasets): use video path metadata helper

* docs(tests): clarify packed video fixture behavior

* test(datasets): create packed videos with episode boundaries

* test(datasets): simplify episode encoding fixture changes

* test(datasets): restrict stream-copy regression to h264

* test(datasets): cover stream-copy and reencode deletion paths

* test(datasets): store open-GOP video as test artifact

* refactor(datasets): unify video episode filtering entry point

* fix(datasets): preserve decode timestamps during stream copy

* test(datasets): build the GOP-alignment test dataset directly

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* test(datasets): drop the unused vcodec parameter from the packed-video helper

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* test(datasets): stop asserting which encode path ran in the packed-video test

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* test(datasets): drop unused packed-video changes from test fixtures

The stream-copy tests build their packed dataset through the recording path, so
create_videos no longer needs per-episode encoding.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(eo1): give the slow Qwen2.5-VL image processor CPU images (#5146)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(eo1): give the slow Qwen2.5-VL image processor CPU images (#5146)

lerobot-rollout, lerobot-train, and the predict_action and
build_inference_frame helpers move the batch to the policy device before
the preprocessor runs. EO-1's Qwen step then passed GPU image tensors to
the default (slow) Qwen2.5-VL image processor, which reads pixels with
NumPy and fails:

    TypeError: can't convert cuda:0 device type tensor to numpy.

lerobot-eval fails the same way with IsaacLab Arena environments, which
return camera images on the GPU. Other environments and the policy
server pass CPU images.

Move the images to the CPU in the Qwen step when the slow processor is
used. The move uses move_state_dict_to_device, which builds new message
containers, so the transition the previous step returned keeps its GPU
images. The fast processor (use_fast_processor=True) already handles GPU
tensors, so its images stay on their device, as before. The preprocessor's
last step still moves its outputs to the policy device, and CPU input is
unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Haoming Song <haomingsong24@gmail.com>
